_notes.dataset: custom_dataset_rahul_Aug30: 545 files, 15 visual categories, assembled from public benchmark sources (OWID charts, UCSF industry documents, arXiv figures, IAM handwriting, RICO screenshots, scene-text photos, French annual-report tables, handwritten C++ study notes, receipts). Registered on this machine 2026-08-30 via register_corpus.py; the earlier registration commit was reverted (17111c7) and this run re-registers it. Golden set generated fresh for this run - no prior run shares this dataset, so nothing here is comparable to the two committed receipts runs.
_notes.golden_persona: Owner decision 2026-08-30: no single person plausibly owns all 15 categories, so the golden set is written under ONE umbrella persona - a CS grad student whose Mac has everything dumped in one place. This keeps questions persona-real (skill Phase 2) and makes cross-category multi-file items legitimate.
_notes.notes_iam_excluded: Owner decision 2026-08-30: the 30 notes_iam files stay INDEXED (realistic distractors) but carry ZERO golden items. They are IAM/LOB handwriting benchmark strips - unrelated sentence fragments with no coherent subject, so no persona-real question can be asked of them. Any retrieval hit on a notes_iam file is therefore a false positive by construction; the retrieval report should treat that slice as pure distractor pressure, not as unmeasured coverage.
_notes.top_k: owner decision 2026-08-30: k=2, matching 20260829T065335Z-receipts-topk2-rerank-off. One knob, both axes - worker.py:294 passes top_k straight into ask(), so 2 files are retrieved AND 2 are fed to the generator. top_k_retrieval_max stays 12 (retrieval-only sweeps; unused by this full run).
_notes.rerank: MAGPIE_RERANK kill-switch; production default is ON - this run deliberately diverges (owner decision 2026-08-30, same rationale as baseline): the cross-encoder scores visual hits against the constant placeholder '(visual match - page N)' (product bug #1), so rerank off = ColQwen's own fusion ranking. false ALSO structurally disables the solo gate (its margin is on cross-encoder score scale); run.py:154 stamps solo_gate_structurally_off. Owner was told this makes the run a rerank+gate change together, not a clean rerank-only test, and chose off.
_notes.solo_margin: 0 = gate off, stated explicitly rather than implied by rerank=false (owner decision 2026-08-30, confirmed when asked). Production default is 2.0; recording 2.0 here would have been a config that lies about the run, since the gate cannot fire at any margin with rerank off.
_notes.rewrite: OFF (owner decision 2026-08-30). Query-side only: worker.py:278 passes it into ask(), and the retrieval sweep at worker.py:442 swaps rewrite_query() for raw_query(). raw_query() (search.py:1013) makes no LLM call, so the wall-clock-contamination failure mode found on receipts (the rewriter injecting the current date into the query string) cannot occur. Keywords are still populated by extract_rare_tokens() (MAGPIE_RARE_TOKENS defaults on), NOT left empty. Does NOT affect the LIST_ALL widener, which classifies on the raw question (search.py:771).
_notes.fast_search: REQUIRED, not a free choice: every one of the 545 files is a jpg/png/pdf, so every golden item carries requires.visual_tier=true and run.py:101 hard-fails the run without it. Production ships visual-tier search OFF; this is a dataset-level override (review #31) and the worker default stays production-faithful False.
_notes.col_model: auto (owner decision 2026-08-30) = this machine resolves ColQwen (>=8GB VRAM / >=24GB unified) or ColSmol. Index-side param, part of the index key; the RESOLVED family is stamped into run.json and the index store meta, so a cross-machine comparison can never silently mix retrievers.
_notes.temperature: evals run at 0 (PLAN 4.2); production settings.json default is 0.7
_notes.local_n_ctx: pinned: .env.example fresh-clone value & shipped-beta ctx; this machine's .env says 65536 and must not leak (PLAN 3)
_notes.prompt_style_and_memory: INERT - neither name is read anywhere under eval_harness/harness/. Carried for provenance symmetry with baseline.json only; they describe nothing about this run's behaviour.
